Find the area between y = 8 \sin x and y = 9 \cos x over the interval \left[0,\pi\right]. Sketch the curves if necessary.

static.solution:
Over the interval [0,\pi], the graphs y = 8\sin x and y = 9 \cos x intersect when 8\sin x = 9 \cos x, i.e., \tan x = \frac{9}{8}, i.e., x=\tan^{-1}(\frac{9}{8})=0.844153986113171.
Let t = \tan^{-1}(\frac{9}{8}).
Over the interval \left[0, t\right], the graph of y = 8\sin x lies below that of y = 9 \cos x. Hence, the area between the two curves is \int_0^{ t}(9 \cos x-8 \sin x)dx \begin{array}{ll} \amp =\left.(9\sin x+8\cos x)\right|_0^{ t} \cr \amp =\left(9\sin t+8\cos t\right)-(9\cdot 0+8\cdot 1)\cr \amp =\left(9\sin t+8\cos t\right)-8 \end{array}
Since t = \tan^{-1}(\frac{9}{8}), we have \tan t = \frac{9}{8}. Considering a rightangle triangle with an angle which opposite side has length 9 and adjacent side has length 8, we see that the hypotenues is \sqrt{145}. Thus \sin t = \frac{9}{\sqrt{145}} and \cos t = \frac{8}{\sqrt{145}}.
9\sin t+8\cos t = \frac{9^2}{\sqrt{145}} + \frac{8^2}{\sqrt{145}} = \frac{9^2+8^2}{\sqrt{145}} = \frac{145}{\sqrt{145}}=\sqrt{145}.
Thus, \int_0^{ t}(9 \cos x-8 \sin x)dx= \sqrt{145}-8.
Over the interval \left[ t,\pi\right], the graph of y = 8\sin x lies above that of y = 9 \cos x. Hence, the area between the two curves is \int^\pi_{ t}(8\sin x - 9 \cos x)dx \begin{array}{ll} \amp =-\left.(9\sin x+8\cos x)\right|^\pi_{ t} \cr \amp =8 + \sqrt{145} \end{array}
Thus the total area is the sum of the above two integrals, which is 2\sqrt{145}.

statement.p: Suppose that the density of cars (in cars per mile) down a 20-mile stretch of the Pennsylvania Turnpike is approximated by \delta(x) = 275 \left(2+\sin\left(4\sqrt{x + 0.175}\right)\right), at a distance x miles from the Breezewood toll plaza. Number = \Sigma
(b) Find the total number of cars on the 20-mile stretch.

static.solution:
(a) Suppose we choose an x, 0\le x\le 20. We approximate the density of the number of the cars between x and x+\Delta x miles as \delta(x) cars per mile. Therefore, the number of cars between x and x+\Delta x is approximately \delta(x)\Delta x. If we slice the 20 mile strip into N slices, we get that the total number of cars is C \approx \Sigma_{i=1}^N \delta(x_i)\Delta x = \Sigma_{i=1}^N \left[ 550 + 275\sin(4\sqrt{x_i + 0.175})\right]\Delta x, where \Delta x =20/N. This is a right-hand approximation; the corresponding left-hand approximation is \Sigma_{i=0}^{N-1}\delta(x_i)\Delta x. We can more loosely write both approximations without referring to the number of steps as C \approx \Sigma \left[ 550 + 275\sin(4\sqrt{x + 0.175})\right]\Delta x.
(b) As N\to\infty, the Riemann sum above approaches the integral C =\int_0^{20} (550 + 275\sin4\sqrt{x + 0.175})\,dx. If we calculate the integral numerically, we find C\approx 10541.3. We can also find the integral exactly as follows: C = \int_0^{20} (550 + 275\sin4\sqrt{x +0.175})\,dx = \int_0^{20} 550\,dx +\int_0^{20} 275\sin4\sqrt{x + 0.175}\,dx = 11000 + 275\int_0^{20}\sin4\sqrt{x +0.175}\,dx. Let w = \sqrt{x +0.175}, so x =w^2 -0.175 and dx =2w\,dw. Then \int_{x=0}^{x=20}\sin 4\sqrt{x +0.175}\,dx = 2\int_{w=\sqrt{0.175}}^{w=\sqrt{20.175}} w\sin 4w\,dw, = 2\left[-{1\over 4}w\cos 4w +{1\over 16}\sin 4w\right] \bigg|_{\sqrt{0.175}}^{\sqrt{20.175}} \approx -1.55. (To find the integral we used the appropriate entry in a table of integrals.) Using this, we have C\approx 11000 + 275(-1.55) \approx 10541.3, which matches our numerical approximation.

We think of the tank as made from infinitely many 'infinitesimal' horizontal slices, with x the vertical distance an infinitesimal slice of the water is from the bottom of the tank (the vertex of the right circular cone).

Now the large right triangle with height 5 and top side length 2 is similar to the right triangle with height x and top side length r. So \frac{5}{2} = \frac{x}{r}\implies 5 r = 2 x or r = {\frac{2}{5}} x.

Each slice at x must be lifted a height h = (5-x) meters, and g=9.8 \frac{meters}{sec^2} . So mgh for each slice is 9.8(1070)\left({\frac{4}{25}} \pi x^2\right)(5-x)\,dx Joules.
